correctness.rationale: Character orthogonality gives J=S/[q(sum |f|²)³], so at 1 the denominator is q⁴. Translation by s/3 reduces the fiber to a binary form of discriminant square class −3, giving N=q−κ+qκ·1_{t=s²/3} and S(1)=q²(q²+q−1). For any real mean-zero h, fixing one coordinate gives L=3Σ_a h(a)χ(D_a); the character Gram matrix has diagonal q(q−1) and vanishing off-diagonal because D_a−D_b runs through the entire field as s varies for a≠b. Thus ΣL²=9q(q−1)Σh². Fixing an ordered pair gives the N-summed curve weights q² on the diagonal and q(q+1) off it, since the residual conic equation has 1 and 1+κ roots, respectively. Hence ΣNQ=−3qΣh². In the real and imaginary directions the numerator's quadratic terms are ΣL²±2ΣNQ; the energy normalization additionally subtracts 3S(1)Σh²/q. Dividing by q⁴ and converting to normalized L² yields the two stated deficit half-Hessian bands. The first variation vanishes at the extremum; conjugation eliminates mixed terms and scaling eliminates the complex constants. A fixed-field uniform Taylor remainder on the slice with mean one gives the sharp local limit, attained asymptotically in imaginary mean-zero directions. Theorem 1.3 and its two cases in §6 verify the imported global bound. At RESULT.md:18 'quadratic-character' denotes the additive chirps defined at line 81, not a multiplicative quadratic character. RESULT.md:23–81 is the all-field replay; the supplied script tests exact counts in five fields but does not implement the separately reported Fourier diagnostics, and it was inspected rather than executed here.

value.rationale: Sharp global control does not quantify near-equality. For the full characteristic-greater-than-three family, this gives the optimal local quadratic coefficient, identifies precisely the weakest directions, and resolves the small but exact 12/q² separation of phase and amplitude curvatures. It is useful fixed-field information independent of any global or uniform-neighborhood stability assertion.
